Looking back at the HeaderDecoder (lines 58, 128), when ANY header is deserialized from RLP (whether validated or not), its Hash field is ALWAYS set to `Keccak.Compute(headerRlp)`. This means:

- Even if a malicious parent header was stored without validation
- When it's retrieved from the database and deserialized
- Its `parent.Hash` field will be the keccak256 of its RLP encoding
- The ValidateParent check `parent.Hash != header.ParentHash` will catch the mismatch
